subsystems.name: Survey and prospecting
subsystems.role: find volatile-rich bodies and work out what they contain.
parts: ground and space telescopes (spectroscopy, stellar occultations)

subsystems.name: Transport and trajectory control
subsystems.role: move a body, or a payload, along a route that takes decades.
parts: gravity assists from the giant planets
solar sails or mass drivers for slow pushes

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: run the plant far from the Sun, where sunlight is roughly 1/900th to 1/2500th of Earth's.

subsystems.name: Extraction plant
subsystems.role: sublimate ice out of the regolith without digging up the whole body.

subsystems.name: Separation and refining
subsystems.role: split a mixed ice into usable nitrogen, methane, ammonia and water.
parts: selective cold traps at stepped temperatures

subsystems.name: Cryogenic storage and transfer
subsystems.role: keep volatiles liquid or solid for years with almost no boil-off.

subsystems.name: Outer-system logistics
subsystems.role: turn a distant ice body into something a settlement or depot can actually use.
parts: refractory residue used as shielding and structure

buildSteps.title: Select a target
buildSteps.detail: Telescopes measure the surface spectra and size of candidate Kuiper Belt objects; a body a few tens to a few hundred kilometres across with abundant nitrogen, methane or water ice is shortlisted.

buildSteps.title: Send a reconnaissance craft
buildSteps.detail: A rendezvous mission — not a flyby — matches the object's orbit after a cruise of 10–30 years, then maps it and measures its ice composition and internal structure. New Horizons showed flybys are possible; stopping there has never been done.

buildSteps.title: Establish power and anchoring
buildSteps.detail: A fission reactor is landed or docked, because solar panels of practical size produce very little at 30–50 AU. The plant is anchored and thermally isolated from the surrounding ice.

buildSteps.title: Build the extraction field
buildSteps.detail: Mirrors or heated panels are deployed over an ice-rich patch. Heat sublimates the top layer under a sealed tent, and the vapour is drawn into cold traps rather than escaping to space.

buildSteps.title: Separate the volatiles
buildSteps.detail: Vapour is passed through a staged series of cold traps held at falling temperatures, so water condenses first, then ammonia, then methane, then nitrogen — each collected in its own tank.

buildSteps.title: Store and transfer
buildSteps.detail: Products go into insulated cryogenic tanks; radiators and sunshades limit heat leak, and small cryocoolers close the remaining gap so nothing boils away over decades.

buildSteps.title: Use the residue
buildSteps.detail: Rock, dust and carbonaceous material left behind is sintered or bagged as radiation shielding, landing pads and structural mass, avoiding the cost of shipping it.

buildSteps.title: Build up the plant
buildSteps.detail: Capacity grows by adding extraction tents, tanks and power modules — ideally manufactured on site from local material, so the facility expands without further launches from Earth.

buildSteps.title: Deliver to a market
buildSteps.detail: Propellant and feedstock are shipped by slow, low-thrust freighters to outer-system depots or habitats — and only in exceptional cases nudged inward, since removing orbital energy is far more expensive than the material is worth.

prerequisites.tech: Nuclear fission power and propulsion for deep space
prerequisites.why: reactors have flown (SNAP-10A in 1965) and are being developed for surface power, but nothing at the tens-to-hundreds-of-kilowatts scale needed for an industrial plant.
no spacecraft has operated unattended for the 20–40 years a Kuiper Belt plant would need without resupply.

prerequisites.tech: Cryogenic storage and transfer in space
prerequisites.why: long-term zero-boil-off storage has been demonstrated only at small scale, and never with nitrogen or methane over decades.
water-ice extraction is being pursued for the Moon and asteroids, but no mission has mined ice in microgravity or at Kuiper Belt temperatures.
gravity assists and slow spirals are routine; the challenge is scaling them to multi-decade missions with heavy payloads.

pathway.milestone: telescopic surveys that catalogue Kuiper Belt objects, plus the New Horizons flybys of Pluto (2015) and Arrokoth (2019)
pathway.unlocks: a rough map of which bodies are rich in nitrogen, methane and water ice.

pathway.milestone: a dedicated rendezvous orbiter (or lander) at a volatile-rich Kuiper Belt object
pathway.unlocks: the first direct measurement of near-surface ice and the first test of long-life deep-space systems.

pathway.milestone: an in-situ extraction demonstration, most likely at a nearer icy body such as a comet or the lunar poles
pathway.unlocks: proven hardware for sublimation, fractional condensation and long-term cryogenic storage.

pathway.milestone: a pilot Kuiper Belt plant run on fission power, supplying propellant to depots in the outer solar system
pathway.unlocks: outer-system transport that no longer depends on propellant launched from Earth.

pathway.milestone: industrial-scale volatile harvesting, potentially supplying nitrogen for atmosphere replacement on engineered worlds
pathway.unlocks: the only known source of volatile mass large enough for planetary-scale engineering — if the cost of moving it ever falls far enough.
